name: Café Leopold
description: A Colaba institution since 1871. Bullet holes from the 2008 attacks still visible on the walls. Serves cold beer, Irani chai, and greasy noodles to a mix of backpackers and old Bombayites.

name: Kyani & Co.
description: A 1904 Irani café tucked in Marine Lines. Marble tables, wooden chairs, and mawa cake that hasn't changed in decades. Regulars order without menus. Very few tourists ever find it.

name: India Gate
description: The war memorial at the heart of Delhi. Surrounded by manicured lawns where families picnic at sunset. One of the most visited monuments in India — and for good reason.

name: Agrasen ki Baoli
description: A 60-step ancient stepwell hidden in the middle of Connaught Place. Completely free, almost always empty. Used to be haunted by locals — now quietly beautiful. Pigeons and silence.

name: Amber Fort
description: The crown jewel of Rajasthan tourism. Imposing hilltop fortress with mirror halls, elephant rides, and sweeping views. Busy but absolutely worth it. Go at 7am to beat the crowds.

name: Galta Ji Monkey Temple
description: A temple complex in the Aravalli hills overrun by hundreds of rhesus monkeys. Sacred pools, Sanskrit inscriptions, sadhus, and very little English signage. Deeply local.

name: Dal Lake
description: The shikara ride on Dal Lake at dawn is one of India's most photographed experiences. Floating markets, houseboats, and snow-dusted mountains reflected on still water.

name: Char Chinar Island
description: A tiny island in the middle of Dal Lake accessible only by shikara. Four ancient Chinar trees, a ruined Mughal garden, and almost no tourists. Locals call it Rupa Lanka.

name: Hampi Ruins
description: The ghostly ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire spread across 26 sq km of boulder-strewn landscape. Sunrise from Matanga Hill is life-changing. Now a major backpacker hub.

name: Anegundi Village
description: Across the Tungabhadra river from Hampi's main circuit. An ancient village older than Hampi itself. Coracle rides, banana groves, women weaving baskets. Almost no tourists cross over.

name: Taj Mahal
description: No introduction needed. One of humanity's greatest architectural achievements. Worth every rupee, every crowd, every hour. Go at sunrise. Go twice.

name: Mehtab Bagh
description: A Mughal moonlit garden directly across the Yamuna from the Taj. The view from here, with the Taj reflected in the river, is better than from inside. Almost no one knows this.

name: Varanasi Ghats
description: The Ganga aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat is one of the most powerful rituals in Hinduism. Thousands gather nightly. Sacred, chaotic, ancient. Nothing prepares you.

name: Tulsi Ghat
description: 3km south of the main ghats. Named after the saint Tulsidas. At 5am, only sadhus, priests, and a handful of locals bathe here. Crumbling temples, incense smoke, absolute silence.

name: Munnar Tea Gardens
description: Rolling green hills carpeted with tea estates at 1600m altitude. Misty mornings, wildlife sightings, and cool air. A classic Kerala hill station that earns its popularity.

name: Lakkam Waterfalls Trail
description: A 45-min trek through shola forest to a waterfall known only to Munnar locals. No signboards, no tea stalls, no tour buses. Sometimes a lone elephant.

name: Golden Temple
description: Harmandir Sahib — the holiest Sikh shrine, shimmering in gold on a sacred pool. Free langar feeds 100,000 people daily. Spiritually overwhelming for everyone, regardless of faith.

name: Partition Museum
description: The world's first museum dedicated to the 1947 Partition. Personal testimonies, artifacts, letters. Deeply moving, rarely crowded, and critically important. Most tourists skip it.

name: Coorg Coffee Estates
description: Coorg's coffee and spice plantations are among India's most scenic. Homestays, trekking, and misty peaks. The Scotland of India — deservedly popular.

name: Iruppu Falls Trail
description: A sacred waterfall at the edge of Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary. The river originates from the Brahmagiri peak. Accessible only by foot. Silent except for Langur monkeys and the falls.
